summary: Iteration 6: SOS safety alerts and Auto Nearest Dispatch. Backend: the new suite test_sos_dispatch.py passed 20/20 (run with -n 0). It covers raise (403/400 rules, duplicate, device vs driver_last_known location, admin and customer notifications), GET my SOS, the admin list role matrix (finance and verification get 403), acknowledge/resolve rules, the sos_active flag being set and then cleared on the booking and on the public live page, and nearest-first waves with 11 TEST_ drivers (ranking, wave sizes 3/5/rest, badge moving one wave earlier, stale location going to wave 2, visible_at at +0/+3/+6 min, notified flags, hidden future offers, early accept returning 400, the background loop notifying due offers within about 30s). I updated 3 iteration-5 tests in test_share_badges_livemap.py that broke because of the intended design change (5 min priority became 3 min waves); now 18 pass and 1 is skipped. Frontend (390x844): the customer SOS flow (button, sheet, note, send, status card, 'Ops Manager (Demo) is handling your SOS' after ERP acknowledge) works. The driver SOS on /trip works. The ERP dashboard sos-banner goes to /erp/sos, and the More menu item more-sos works too. Filters, map, call buttons, acknowledge and resolve all work; the resolve button stays disabled until a note is typed. public-sos-banner shows on /live/{token}. offer-distance shows '0.7 km from you · you're among the nearest'. All SOS alerts I created are resolved and the TEST_ drivers and bookings are cleaned up.

minor.issue: No wave-0 fallback. If no eligible driver has a fresh (<30 min) location, every offer lands in wave 2 (badge holders in wave 1), so nobody sees the booking for 3-6 minutes even when there is no competition. Reproduced: Bengaluru badge driver with a stale location got visible_at +180s. Suggest shifting waves so the lowest non-empty wave becomes visible right away.
Duplicate check is find-then-insert, not atomic. Two quick taps can create 2 OPEN alerts from the same side. Low risk because the UI disables the button while busy.

ui_bugs.issue: The app never sends the device lat/lng; the body is only {note}. A customer SOS falls back to the driver's last known location, which was 6+ hours old in the test (ERP showed 'Driver's last known location · 3:27 am'). Get the current position with expo-location when permission is granted and send lat/lng. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/SosButton.tsx:28

issues: The 'Customer Ananya' call button label wraps onto 2 lines at 390px width (small Btn in a row with flex:1).
The map marker always uses kind 'driver' (car icon), even when the location came from the customer's phone.
Resolved alerts still show a red, emphasized call-customer button; consider muting the call buttons for RESOLVED alerts.
The resolve note is not cleared when the sheet is closed without resolving, so it carries over to the next alert.
Shows 'Updated 383 min ago' next to 'Driver arriving in ~9 min'. A stale location still drives a confident ETA.

action_items: SosButton: request the location with expo-location (getCurrentPositionAsync, short timeout, then fall back) and send {note, lat, lng}. This matters most for customer-raised SOS.
broadcast_offers: if wave 0 is empty after ranking, promote the next non-empty wave to visible immediately (and set notified=true) so bookings are not hidden for 3-6 min.
Optional: make the SOS duplicate check atomic (unique partial index on booking_id+raised_by_role for OPEN/ACKNOWLEDGED, or find_one_and_update with upsert).
Minor UI: fix the call-button label wrapping on /erp/sos, use a customer-style marker for device locations, clear the resolve note when the sheet closes.
critical_code_review_comments: sos_routes.raise_sos: the driver_location dict comprehension assumes the keys lat/lng/at all exist (KeyError risk if older docs lack 'at').
GET /api/bookings/{id}/sos returns 404 (not 403) for non-participants. That is acceptable and avoids leaking whether a booking exists.
GET /api/admin/sos?status=<unknown> silently returns an empty list; validating the status would be cleaner.
No deprecated Expo packages (expo-av, expo-barcode-scanner, expo-background-fetch) found.
